notes: Densities from Sunnyvale Municipal Code Title 19 (Zoning). Max densities are base maximums; density bonuses may apply per California Government Code Sections 65915-65918 and local incentive programs. Where the code specifies only a maximum, min_density is listed as 0 (no explicit minimum unless noted). For commercial/industrial/public facilities zones, residential is generally not a permitted primary use (density 0) unless the General Plan or a combining district allows it.

R-0.description: Low Density Residential. Reserved for single-family detached homes. Max 7 du/ac.

R-1.description: Low Density Residential. Reserved for single-family detached homes. Max 7 du/ac.

R-1.7/PD.description: Low-Medium Density Residential (Planned Development). Small-lot residential development. Must be combined with PD combining district. Max 14 du/ac.

R-2.description: Low-Medium Density Residential. Allows duplexes and small multi-family. Max 12 du/ac.

R-3.description: Medium Density Residential. Allows multi-family residential. Max 24 du/ac.

R-4.description: High Density Residential. Allows multi-family residential. Max 36 du/ac.

R-5.description: High Density Residential and Office. Allows multi-family residential alone or in combination with hotels/motels. Max 45 du/ac.

R-MH.description: Residential-Mobile Home. Reserved for mobile home parks and incidental uses. Max 12 du/ac of mobile home park area.

C-1.description: Neighborhood Business. Retail commercial and service facilities for adjacent residential areas. Residential not a primary permitted use; may be allowed under state law consistent with General Plan density.

C-2.description: Highway Business. Retail commercial, tourist accommodations, and highway-oriented service facilities. Residential not a primary permitted use; may be allowed under state law consistent with General Plan density.

M-S.description: Industrial and Service. Offices, research, limited manufacturing, hotels/motels, restaurants, financial uses, retail sales and services. Residential not a primary permitted use (see ITR combining district for conversion allowance).

M-3.description: General Industrial. Offices, research, general manufacturing and compatible uses. Residential not permitted.

O.description: Office. Administrative, professional and research offices; residential may be allowed with a use permit if the General Plan designates the site as Village Mixed Use (average ~18 du/ac across Village Centers per General Plan). Base zoning does not establish an independent residential density.

P-F.description: Public Facilities. Governmental, public utility, and educational buildings and facilities. Residential not a primary permitted use.

DSP.description: Downtown Specific Plan District (Chapter 19.28). Divided into subdistricts (blocks). General Plan maximum allowed density is 65 du/ac. Additional density possible through local/state density bonus or community benefits programs.

ECR-R3.description: El Camino Real - Medium Density Residential (Chapter 19.36). Max 24 du/ac, consistent with citywide R-3 district.

ECR-MU-24.description: El Camino Real - Mixed Use, 24 du/ac classification. Base maximum density of 24 du/ac per Table 19.36.070.

ECR-MU-36.description: El Camino Real - Mixed Use, 36 du/ac classification. Base maximum density of 36 du/ac per Table 19.36.070.

ECR-MU-54.description: El Camino Real - Mixed Use, 54 du/ac classification. Base maximum density of 54 du/ac per Table 19.36.070.

ECR-MU-72.description: El Camino Real - Mixed Use, 72 du/ac classification. Base maximum density of 72 du/ac per Table 19.36.070.

ECR-MU-90.description: El Camino Real - Mixed Use, 90 du/ac classification. Base maximum density of 90 du/ac per Table 19.36.070. Higher densities available through Incentives Program for community benefits.

MP-MU.description: Moffett Park - Mixed Use (Chapter 19.29). Allows standalone residential, standalone office, or mixed-use. Minimum residential density of 36 du/ac (consistent with R-4). Maximum density per the Moffett Park Specific Plan; up to ~100 du/ac anticipated for high-density sites.

MP-I.description: Moffett Park - Industrial (Chapter 19.29). Industrial and office uses. Residential not a primary permitted use in this subdistrict.

General Business.description: General Business (GIS alias). Maps to C-1/C-2 commercial zones. Residential not a primary permitted use.

Highway Commercial.description: Highway Commercial (GIS alias). Maps to C-2 Highway Business. Retail commercial, tourist accommodations, and highway-oriented service facilities. Residential not a primary permitted use.

Industrial.description: Industrial (GIS alias). Maps to M-S/M-3 Industrial zones. Residential not permitted.

Lakefront.description: Lakefront (GIS alias). Special district; treated as non-residential for density purposes.

Local Retail.description: Local Retail (GIS alias). Maps to C-1 Neighborhood Business. Residential not a primary permitted use.

Multifamily Residential.description: Multifamily Residential (GIS alias). Maps to R-3/R-4 multi-family residential zones. Max density up to 36 du/ac depending on subdistrict.

Planned Development.description: Planned Development (GIS alias). Maps to PD combining district. Density depends on underlying zoning and approved plan; up to 14 du/ac for R-1.7/PD.

Single Family - 1.description: Single Family - 1 (GIS alias). Maps to R-0/R-1 Low Density Residential. Max 7 du/ac.

Single Family - 2.description: Single Family - 2 (GIS alias). Maps to R-0/R-1 Low Density Residential. Max 7 du/ac.

Single Family - 3.description: Single Family - 3 (GIS alias). Maps to R-1.5 Low-Medium Density Residential. Max 10 du/ac.

Single Family - 4.description: Single Family - 4 (GIS alias). Maps to R-2 Low-Medium Density Residential. Max 12 du/ac.

Single Family - 5.description: Single Family - 5 (GIS alias). Maps to R-2/R-MH density range. Max 12 du/ac.

PD.description: Planned Development combining district. May be combined with base zoning districts to allow flexible site design; does not independently change density.

ITR.description: Industrial to Residential combining district. Allows industrial, office, commercial and residential uses within the same zoning district; permits gradual conversion from industrial/office/commercial to residential use. Residential density governed by the applicable General Plan designation.

HH.description: Heritage Housing combining district. Preserves historic residential neighborhood character; does not change underlying density limits.

S.description: Single-Story combining district. May be combined with R-0, R-1, and R-2. Preserves single-story neighborhood character; does not change underlying density limits.
